# KV Cache: Enabling Efficient Long-Context Inference

## What Is KV Cache?

KV cache is an optimization technique used during autoregressive inference in transformer-based language models. It stores the key and value matrices from previous token positions, avoiding redundant recomputation as the model generates each new token. This mechanism is fundamental to making long-context applications practical.

## How Attention Creates Redundancy

To understand why KV cache matters, consider how standard attention works during generation. When processing a sequence, the attention mechanism computes query vectors for the current token and compares them against key vectors from all previous positions to determine attention weights. These comparisons produce weighted sums of value vectors, which feed into subsequent layers.

In naive inference, each new token requires recomputing key and value matrices for the entire sequence seen so far. If you've generated 1,000 tokens and want to process token 1,001, you recalculate keys and values for all 1,000 previous positions even though they haven't changed. This creates O(n²) computational complexity relative to sequence length, where n is the number of tokens processed.

# KV Cache: Enabling Efficient Long-Context Inference

## The Self-Attention Bottleneck

Modern large language models rely on the self-attention mechanism to process sequences of tokens. At each position, the model computes attention scores between the current token and all previous tokens in the sequence. This operation requires three key components: the query (Q), which represents what information the current token seeks; the key (K), which represents what information each token offers; and the value (V), which holds the actual content to be retrieved.

During autoregressive generation, the model generates one token at a time, with each new token depending on all previously generated tokens. Consider a sequence of length n—the model must compute attention for each position, performing matrix multiplications that scale quadratically with sequence length. For a 4,096-token context, this means computing attention over more than 16 million token pairs per attention head. Without optimization, processing long sequences becomes computationally prohibitive.

## How KV Cache Solves This

The KV cache optimizes this process by recognizing a fundamental asymmetry in autoregressive generation. While queries are unique to each generation step, keys and values for previously processed tokens never change. Once the model has computed the K and V matrices for a token, those matrices remain fixed for all subsequent generation steps.
